text:
Anna: heads-up — customer 'FinSight' reported a big p99 jump on /v1/chat yesterday evening, lots of 504s. They say it started after they switched to long-context mode (~32k).
Sam: digging into metrics now. which region?
Anna: eu-west1, high-throughput tenant. I saw a correlation with GPU memory spiking on the pod group serving that model variant.
Priya: I pulled the prometheus graphs — p50 steady, p95/p99 doubled from ~400ms to ~1.2s and error rate up ~3%. GPU memory usage slowly climbed until OOMs started happening.
Zach: logs from the runtime show repeated allocation retries and `CUDARuntimeError: out of memory` in the attention kernel. Also a bunch of warnings: "KV cache growth: session_id=... size=XXMB".
Anna: sounds like KV cache + fragmentation. customer long-lived conversations, many tokens appended, KV never evicted.
Sam: confirmed. KV entries per-session grew linearly. Also allocator fragmentation — free memory exists but split into tiny chunks.
Priya: immediate mitigation suggestions?
Zach: short list: 1) throttle prefix/KV caching for that tenant (set max_prefix_tokens), 2) roll to quantized model variant to reduce memory, 3) bump node pool for that shard (add GPUs) to alleviate pressure, 4) quick rolling restart of pods to compact allocator.
Anna: can we do (1) quickly? route that tenant to a throttle rule.
Sam: yes — we have a per-tenant cache policy. I can set `max_cached_prefix_tokens=4096` for them. Doing it now.
infra-bot: deploy started by Sam — cache-policy update for tenant FinSight (id: fin-237)
Sam: done — policy applied. Watching metrics.
Priya: also started a canary scale-up (+2 g4dn instances) for the shard. infra-bot reported provisioning.
Zach: in the mid-term we should tune CUDA allocator flags. Proposed env: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` — helps with fragmentation by avoiding lots of tiny splits.
Anna: any downside?
Zach: might increase peak usage slightly, but reduces failed small allocations and fragmentation churn. We should test on staging.
Priya: Another change: enable periodic KV eviction for inactive sessions (`kv:ttl=48h` -> maybe lower to 6-12h for this tenant). That will reduce long-term growth.
Sam: set TTL to 12h for FinSight as emergency config.
Anna: good. What about model runtime changes? compaction?
Zach: PyTorch doesn't compact GPU memory easily. `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` doesn't defragment. But restarting the process releases memory back to the OS and defragments. We can implement staggered rolling restarts tied to memory heuristics: if fragmentation metric > threshold, restart pod.
Priya: we should be careful — restarts cause in-flight latency. Use canary restarts and set `max_unavailable=1`.
Sam: for immediate customer-facing relief I also added a fallback routing to the cheaper quantized endpoint for requests that exceed a token threshold (>=16k). This will reduce allocation footprint per request.
Anna: thanks. Can we capture repro steps so Eng-ML can reproduce fragmentation and test allocator tweaks?
Zach: repro plan (quick):
```
# spawn 300 concurrent chat sessions each appending 2k tokens every 30s for 40 minutes
python tools/loadgen.py --model chat-32k --sessions 300 --append-size 2048 --interval 30 --duration 2400 --tenant fin-237 --region eu-west1
```
Collect: GPU free/used, fragmentation metric (we added `gpu_allocator_fragmentation_ratio`), runtime logs, and per-session KV sizes.
Priya: I'll run this in staging with a smaller scale (50 sessions) and try the `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` tweak.
Sam: notes on quick logs we saw:
```
2026-01-12T18:22:14Z runtime[handler]: alloc retry 3 (size=12.3MB) -> failed
2026-01-12T18:22:14Z runtime[handler]: attention_kernel: cudnn error: CUDARuntimeError: out of memory
2026-01-12T18:22:14Z runtime[kv]: session=abcd size=32456KB
```
Zach: also saw increased page faults on the host after a pod OOM, maybe cuda-mig thrash? worth checking host-level OOM killer logs.
Anna: action items: Sam -> applied throttle + routing fallback + monitor (done). Priya -> run staging repro + try allocator env tweak, report results. Zach -> create a small patch for eviction TTL per-tenant and instrumentation for fragmentation ratio. I'll coordinate customer comms.
Sam: metrics are trending down already — GPU memory slope flattened, p99 dropping from 1.2s -> ~620ms within 12 minutes.
Priya: stage run starting now with `max_split_size_mb:128` and baseline without it. Will post results in this thread.
Zach: I'll open an internal ticket ENG-RUNTIME-4567 with logs + suggested allocator knob changes and a checklist for long-term fixes (auto-eviction, adaptive kv caps, rolling restart heuristics).
Anna: thanks all. Let's keep the thread updated — if latency stabilizes for 30m we can mark as mitigated and schedule a postmortem on the tenant impact and longer-term runtime fixes. :thumbsup:
__notes: This file is a synthetic realistic Slack thread about GPU memory pressure, KV cache growth, fragmentation, and mitigations. Contains repro steps, commands, metrics, and action items.
